options.label: Piranesi front elevation
options.description: Dense engraved linework shows the portico and dome, with the later bell towers deliberately omitted.
options.credit: Francesco Piranesi; Raccolta de’ tempj antichi, 1790, reproduced in Firmin Didot Frères, Opere, vol. 6, 1835–1839. University of Tokyo scan via Wikimedia Commons.
options.altText: Frontal engraved elevation of the Pantheon, with its eight-column portico beneath a triangular pediment and the rotunda behind.
options.license: Public domain / PD-Art and Public Domain Mark as recorded by Wikimedia Commons.
options.sourceNotes: The source record dates this distinct etching to 1790. The scan comes from the 1835–1839 collected edition, not an original Roman architectural document. Full original sheet and annotations retained. Plate V is explicitly titled an elevation of the then-present Pantheon without the modern bell towers. It is a historical analytical view, not an unchanged snapshot of the building in 1790.
